title: Getting started with lsastrat
text: lsastrat turns large-scale assessment (LSA) data — PISA, TIMSS, PIRLS — stratification inequality quantities education researchers report, returns first-class objects. handles two features make LSA data awkward: Plausible values (PVs). Achievement reported several imputed draws, single score. Every estimator computed PV results combined Rubin’s (1987) rules, measurement uncertainty enters standard error. Replicate weights. Complex sampling means variance must estimated replicate weights (BRR/Fay PISA; JK2 TIMSS/PIRLS) , segregation indices, clustered bootstrap. Inference uses t reference Rubin degrees freedom (normal), matters LSA studies provide 5 10 plausible values. examples use pisa_mini, fully simulated PISA-like data set bundled package (real PISA data). 10 plausible values mathematics reading (PV1MATH…PV10MATH), final weight (W_FSTUWT), 64 Fay BRR replicate weights (W_FSTURWT1…W_FSTURWT64), background variables.
code: reps <- paste0("W_FSTURWT", 1:64) math <- paste0("PV", 1:10, "MATH")

title: Getting started with lsastrat
text: social_gradient() follows OECD definition: slope score-point change per one unit socio-economic index (ESCS), strength percentage achievement variance explains (R² × 100), curvature optional quadratic term. result behaves like model object:
code: g <- social_gradient(pisa_mini, achievement = math, escs = "ESCS",                      weight = "W_FSTUWT", repweights = reps) g #> Socio-economic achievement gradient #>   SES index: ESCS   |   10 plausible value(s)   |   n = 2048 #>   Variance:  BRR, 64 replicate weights (+ PV imputation); t reference #>  #>  #>           Estimate Std.Error     t    df       p #> slope       41.357     1.831 22.59 399.4 2.1e-73 #> strength    20.189     1.799 11.22 389.1 1.7e-25 #> curvature    1.025     1.597  0.64 406.7 5.2e-01 #>  #> slope = score points per 1 unit of ESCS; strength = % variance explained (R^2 x 100) coef(g) #>     slope  strength curvature  #> 41.357302 20.188700  1.025083 confint(g) #>               2.5 %    97.5 % #> slope     37.758539 44.956065 #> strength  16.651036 23.726363 #> curvature -2.113944  4.164111 plot(g)

title: Getting started with lsastrat
text: segregation_index() reports family indices used stratification research. Pass categorical group social segregation: entropy dissimilarity indices upward-biased schools small — exactly LSA case. variance = "bootstrap" two-stage clustered bootstrap estimates removes bias (debias = TRUE) gives design-correct standard error. replicate weights can instead use directly (bias correction): academic segregation, define group achievement threshold; index pooled across plausible values:
code: segregation_index(pisa_mini, unit = "school_id", group = "IMMIG",                   weight = "W_FSTUWT", variance = "bootstrap",                   n_boot = 99, boot_seed = 1) #> Segregation indices (social segregation) #>   unit: school_id  |  128 units  |  3 group(s)  |  minority: first_gen #>   Variance: clustered bootstrap (B=99, cluster=school_id), bias-corrected #>  #>  #>           Estimate Std.Error     t  df       p #> D            0.578     0.037 15.45 Inf 7.8e-54 #> S            0.554     0.040 13.83 Inf 1.7e-43 #> isolation    0.097     0.027  3.55 Inf 3.8e-04 #> Hutchens     0.362     0.036  9.97 Inf 2.2e-23 #> H            0.095     0.017  5.50 Inf 3.9e-08 #> M            0.074     0.016  4.59 Inf 4.3e-06 segregation_index(pisa_mini, unit = "school_id", group = "IMMIG",                   weight = "W_FSTUWT", repweights = reps,                   indices = c("D", "H", "M")) #> Segregation indices (social segregation) #>   unit: school_id  |  128 units  |  3 group(s)  |  minority: first_gen #>   Variance: BRR, 64 replicate weights; t reference #>  #>  #>   Estimate Std.Error     t  df       p #> D    0.658     0.040 16.47 Inf 6.2e-61 #> H    0.157     0.012 13.12 Inf 2.5e-39 #> M    0.122     0.011 11.39 Inf 4.8e-30 segregation_index(pisa_mini, unit = "school_id", achievement = math,                   cutoff = 480, indices = c("D", "H"),                   variance = "bootstrap", n_boot = 99, boot_seed = 1) #> No `weight` supplied; using equal weights. #> Segregation indices (academic segregation) #>   unit: school_id  |  128 units  |  2 group(s)  |  minority: below #>   Variance: clustered bootstrap (B=99, cluster=school_id), bias-corrected (+ PV imputation) #>  #>  #>   Estimate Std.Error    t    df       p #> D    0.218     0.026 8.39 109.0 1.9e-13 #> H    0.052     0.019 2.83 475.3 4.9e-03

what: Stratification and Inequality Metrics for Large-Scale Assessment Data
title: Stratification and Inequality Metrics for Large-Scale Assessment Data
text: Stratification inequality metrics large-scale assessment (LSA) data. lsastrat computes educational-stratification quantities PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS researchers normally hand-assemble, returns first-class objects correct plausible-value pooling (Rubin’s rules) replicate-weight variance (BRR/Fay, JK2, JK1): social_gradient() — socio-economic achievement gradient (slope, strength = R² × 100, curvature). segregation_index() — school segregation indices (Dissimilarity, Gorard’s S, isolation, Hutchens, Theil’s H, mutual information) two-stage clustered bootstrap finite-sample bias correction. ieop() — Ferreira–Gignoux decomposition inequality educational opportunity. General LSA packages (EdSurvey, intsvy, BIFIEsurvey, RALSA, OECD’s Rrepest) handle plausible values replicate weights expose generic estimators (means, regression, correlation); none emits stratification quantities labelled outputs. lsastrat fills gap designed sit alongside engines.

title: Inequality of educational opportunity (Ferreira-Gignoux) — ieop
text: Computes Ferreira-Gignoux (2014) measure inequality educational opportunity (IOp): share achievement inequality attributable pre-determined circumstances (family background, gender, migration status, similar variables outside student's control). \(R^2\) regression achievement circumstance vector, using variance inequality index.

title: Inequality of educational opportunity (Ferreira-Gignoux) — ieop
code: ieop(   data,   achievement,   circumstances,   weight = NULL,   repweights = NULL,   rep_method = c("BRR", "JK2", "JK1"),   fay = 0.5,   statistics = c("iop", "iop_adj", "explained_var", "total_var"),   level = 0.95 )

title: Inequality of educational opportunity (Ferreira-Gignoux) — ieop
text: data data frame student-level records. achievement Character vector achievement plausible-value columns. circumstances Character vector circumstance columns (vector \(C\)). Character/factor columns treated categorical; numeric columns enter linearly. canonical PISA application (Ferreira & Gignoux, 2014) uses gender, parental education occupation, books household possessions, language home migration status. weight Name final student weight column. NULL, equal weights used (message). repweights Optional character vector replicate-weight columns. rep_method, fay Replication design Fay factor; see rep_factor(). statistics quantities return: "iop" (relative IOp = raw \(R^2\)), "iop_adj" (df-adjusted relative IOp), "explained_var" (absolute IOp) "total_var" (total achievement variance). level Confidence level stored interval (default 0.95).

title: Inequality of educational opportunity (Ferreira-Gignoux) — ieop
text: object class "ieop" / "lsastrat_estimate" (see lsastrat_estimate methods).

title: Inequality of educational opportunity (Ferreira-Gignoux) — ieop
text: Following Ferreira & Gignoux, variance inequality measure choice , unlike Gini coefficient mean log deviation, ordinally invariant affine standardisation assessment scores undergo. relative IOp $$IOp = \mathrm{Var}(\hat y) / \mathrm{Var}(y) = R^2,$$ ratio circumstance-predicted ("smoothed") achievement variance total achievement variance. absolute IOp \(\mathrm{Var}(\hat y)\) squared score points.

title: Inequality of educational opportunity (Ferreira-Gignoux) — ieop
text: raw \(R^2\) upper bound: mechanically inflated circumstance vector expands many dummy columns (Ferreira & Gignoux, 2014). ieop() therefore also reports iop_adj, degrees--freedom adjusted relative IOp, $$1 - (1 - R^2)\,\frac{n_\mathrm{eff} - 1}{n_\mathrm{eff} - k},$$ \(n_\mathrm{eff}\) Kish's weighted effective sample size \(k\) number estimated parameters, warns \(k\) large relative \(n_\mathrm{eff}\). Cross-fitted / sample-split IOp planned future release. Achievement supplied plausible values pooled Rubin's rules; standard errors design-based replicate weights given.

title: Inequality of educational opportunity (Ferreira-Gignoux) — ieop
text: Ferreira, F. H. G. & Gignoux, J. (2014). measurement educational inequality: Achievement opportunity. World Bank Economic Review, 28(2), 210-246.

title: Pool point estimates and variances across plausible values (Rubin's rules) — pool_pv
text: Combines per-plausible-value point estimates (design-based) sampling variances single estimate, standard error, \(t\)-reference test following multiple-imputation combining rules Rubin (1987).

title: Pool point estimates and variances across plausible values (Rubin's rules) — pool_pv
text: estimates Numeric vector per-PV point estimates (\(\hat\theta_p\)), length m = number plausible values. variances Numeric vector per-PV sampling variances (\(U_p\)), length. Pass zeros design-based variance available (result imputation variance ). non-finite entry propagates NA standard error rather error. level Confidence level returned interval (default 0.95).

title: Pool point estimates and variances across plausible values (Rubin's rules) — pool_pv
text: named list: estimate, se, statistic (estimate / se), df (Rubin degrees freedom), p (two-sided), ci_lo, ci_hi, var_sampling (\(\bar U\)), var_imputation (\((1 + 1/m) B\) term), m.

title: Pool point estimates and variances across plausible values (Rubin's rules) — pool_pv
text: m plausible values pooled estimate mean per-PV estimates. total variance $$T = \bar U + (1 + 1/m) B,$$ \(\bar U\) mean sampling variance (within-imputation) \(B\) -PV variance (imputation/measurement component). Inference uses \(t\) reference Rubin's degrees freedom $$\nu = (m - 1)\left(1 + \frac{\bar U}{(1 + 1/m) B}\right)^2,$$ correctly widens intervals imputation component non-negligible relative sampling component (usual case small number plausible values, 5 10, PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS). imputation variance (single plausible value) reference reduces normal (\(\nu = \infty\)); sampling variance reference \(t\) \(m - 1\) degrees freedom.

title: Pool point estimates and variances across plausible values (Rubin's rules) — pool_pv

title: Replicate-weight variance factors — rep_factor
text: BRR/Fay: \(c = 1 / (R (1 - k)^2)\), k fay. fay = 0 ordinary BRR (\(1/R\)); fay = 0.5 (PISA) \(4/R\). JK2 (IEA paired-zone construction): \(c = 1\). JK1 (single-stratum / equal-zone): \(c = (R - 1) / R\).

title: School segregation indices for large-scale assessment data — segregation_index
text: Computes family segregation indices used educational stratification research – measuring unevenly student groups distributed across schools (nesting unit) – survey-weighted counts, plausible-value pooling achievement-based groups, choice variance estimator: replicate weights clustered bootstrap finite-sample bias correction.

title: School segregation indices for large-scale assessment data — segregation_index
code: segregation_index(   data,   unit,   group = NULL,   achievement = NULL,   cutoff = NULL,   indices = c("D", "S", "isolation", "Hutchens", "H", "M"),   minority = NULL,   weight = NULL,   repweights = NULL,   rep_method = c("BRR", "JK2", "JK1"),   fay = 0.5,   variance = c("replicate", "bootstrap", "none"),   n_boot = 200L,   debias = TRUE,   boot_cluster = NULL,   boot_seed = NULL,   level = 0.95 )

title: School segregation indices for large-scale assessment data — segregation_index
text: data data frame student-level records. unit Name school / nesting-unit identifier column. group Name categorical group-membership column. Mutually exclusive achievement/cutoff. achievement Character vector plausible-value column names, used cutoff define achievement-based (academic) group. cutoff Numeric threshold; students achievement < cutoff form "" group. indices indices return. "D" (dissimilarity), "S" (Gorard's segregation index), "isolation" (minority isolation), "Hutchens" (square-root index), "H" (Theil's information / entropy index) "M" (mutual information). H M support two groups; D, S, isolation Hutchens compare minority group rest. minority group level minority binary indices. Defaults least frequent (weighted) level. weight Name final student weight column. NULL, equal weights used (message). repweights Optional character vector replicate-weight columns (used variance = "replicate"). rep_method, fay Replication design Fay factor; see rep_factor(). variance Variance estimator: "replicate" (default repweights supplied), "bootstrap" (default otherwise), "none" (point estimates ). n_boot Number bootstrap resamples (default 200). debias Logical; apply bootstrap bias correction variance = "bootstrap" (default TRUE). boot_cluster Name column defining stage-one bootstrap clusters (primary sampling units); defaults unit. boot_seed Optional integer seed reproducible bootstrap draws (global RNG state restored exit). level Confidence level stored interval (default 0.95).

title: School segregation indices for large-scale assessment data — segregation_index
text: object class "segregation" / "lsastrat_estimate" (see lsastrat_estimate methods): coefficients data frame (one row per index) plus metadata.

title: School segregation indices for large-scale assessment data — segregation_index
text: Two ways define group: Social segregation: pass categorical group column (e.g. immigrant-background flag, disadvantaged/advantaged ESCS split). Academic segregation: pass achievement (vector plausible-value columns) together cutoff; students scoring cutoff form minority group, index pooled across plausible values.

title: School segregation indices for large-scale assessment data — segregation_index
text: entropy dissimilarity indices (M, H, D, Gorard's S, Hutchens) positively biased finite samples, large-scale assessments – tens students sampled per school across many schools – worst case. variance = "bootstrap" two-stage clustered bootstrap used: stage one resamples whole clusters (design level, giving design-correct sampling variance) stage two resamples students within drawn cluster (within-school fluctuation drives finite-sample bias). bootstrap bias estimate subtracted debias = TRUE (Elbers, 2023). variance = "replicate" supplied replicate weights give sampling variance bias correction applied; point estimates (upward-biased) plug-values, bootstrap variance recommended bias concern.

Entropy-based segregation indices. Sociological Methodology, 41(1). Elbers, B. (2023). method studying differences segregation. Sociological Methods & Research (R package segregation).

title: Socio-economic achievement gradient — social_gradient
text: Computes socio-economic gradient achievement large-scale assessment data, following OECD PISA definition: slope score-point change achievement per one-unit change socio-economic index (e.g. ESCS), strength percentage achievement variance explained socio-economic status (\(R^2 \times 100\)). Used repweights supplied. fay Fay adjustment BRR (PISA uses 0.5); see rep_factor(). curvature Logical; TRUE (default) also fit quadratic model report curvature (ESCS-squared) coefficient. level Confidence level stored interval (default 0.95).
